formulations.note: Contains benzalkonium chloride. Fluticasone furoate is a different substance from fluticasone propionate.

src.q: Each spray actuation delivers 27.5 micrograms of fluticasone furoate
This medicinal product contains benzalkonium chloride.

items.t: Symptoms of allergic rhinitis in adults, adolescents and children 6 years and over.

src.q: Avamys is indicated in adults, adolescents and children (6 years and over)
Avamys is indicated for the treatment of the symptoms of allergic rhinitis.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions stated in the UK nasal spray SmPC checked.

items.t: Start with 2 sprays in each nostril once daily (110 micrograms a day); once controlled, 1 spray each nostril once daily (55 micrograms) may be enough. Use the lowest effective dose; limit treatment to the period of allergen exposure.
items.tag: Allergic rhinitis, adults and adolescents 12 years and over

src.q: The recommended starting dose is two spray actuations (27.5 micrograms of fluticasone furoate per spray actuation) in each nostril once daily (total daily dose, 110 micrograms).
dose reduction to one spray actuation in each nostril (total daily dose 55 micrograms) may be effective for maintenance
The duration of treatment should be restricted to the period that corresponds to allergenic exposure.

items.t: 6-11 years: 1 spray in each nostril once daily (55 micrograms); may go up to 2 sprays each nostril (110 micrograms) if needed, then back to 1 spray once controlled. Not established under 6 years.

src.q: The recommended starting dose is one spray actuation (27.5 micrograms of fluticasone furoate per spray actuation) in each nostril once daily (total daily dose, 55 micrograms).
may use two spray actuations in each nostril once daily (total daily dose, 110 micrograms)
The safety and efficacy of Avamys in children under the age of 6 years has not been established.

items.t: Growth velocity fell (-0.27 cm a year) in children on 110 micrograms daily for one year: keep children on the lowest effective dose and monitor growth on prolonged treatment.

src.q: A reduction in growth velocity has been observed in children treated with fluticasone furoate 110 micrograms daily for one year
children should be maintained on the lowest possible efficacious dose which delivers adequate symptom control

items.t: Hypersensitivity to fluticasone furoate or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Systemic steroid effects possible, mainly at high doses for long periods. Above-recommended doses can cause adrenal suppression: consider systemic steroid cover during stress or elective surgery. Consider the total corticosteroid load when other steroid forms are used.

src.q: Systemic effects of nasal corticosteroid may occur, particularly at high doses prescribed for prolonged periods.
the total systemic burden of corticosteroids should be considered whenever other forms of corticosteroid treatment are prescribed concurrently

items.t: Care when transferring from systemic steroids if adrenal function may be impaired.

src.q: If there is any reason to believe that adrenal function is impaired, care must be taken when transferring patients from systemic steroid treatment to fluticasone furoate.

items.t: Blurred vision or other visual disturbance: consider referral to an ophthalmologist.

src.q: the patient should be considered for referral to an ophthalmologist for evaluation of possible causes

items.t: Ritonavir: co-administration not recommended (increased systemic exposure).

src.q: Concomitant administration with ritonavir is not recommended because of the risk of increased systemic exposure of fluticasone furoate

items.t: Potent CYP3A inhibitors, including cobicistat-containing products: caution; avoid unless the benefit outweighs the increased risk of systemic steroid effects, and if used monitor for them. Ritonavir: not recommended. Ketoconazole caused only a small rise in exposure without a significant cortisol change in a study.

src.q: Caution is recommended when co-administering fluticasone furoate with potent CYP3A inhibitors including cobicistat-containing products
Co-administration should be avoided unless the benefit outweighs the increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects
This small increase in exposure did not result in a statistically significant difference in 24 hour serum cortisol levels between the two groups.

items.t: Not expected to affect the CYP450 metabolism of other medicines at nasal doses.

src.q: there is no theoretical basis for anticipating metabolic interactions between fluticasone furoate and the cytochrome P450 mediated metabolism of other compounds at clinically relevant intranasal doses

items.t: No dose adjustment needed.

src.q: Renal Impairment No dose adjustment is required in this population

items.t: No dose adjustment needed in hepatic impairment.

src.q: No dose adjustment is required in patients with hepatic impairment

items.t: SmPC: no adequate human data; animal effects at high systemic exposure are unlikely to be relevant at nasal doses. Use only if the benefit to the mother outweighs the possible risk.

src.q: This is not likely to be relevant for humans given recommended nasal doses which results in minimal systemic exposure
Fluticasone furoate should be used in pregnancy only if the benefits to the mother outweigh the potential risks to the foetus or child.

items.t: SPS: intranasal corticosteroids (fluticasone given as an example) can be considered for hay fever in pregnancy if non-drug measures are not enough; they are the most effective rhinitis treatment.

src.q: intranasal corticosteroids (for example, fluticasone) can be considered if non-pharmacological management is insufficient
Intranasal corticosteroids are also the most effective treatment for allergic rhinitis.

items.t: SmPC: excretion in milk unknown; consider only if the expected benefit to the mother is greater than any possible risk to the child.

src.q: Administration of fluticasone furoate to women who are breast-feeding should only be considered if the expected benefit to the mother is greater than any possible risk to the child.

items.t: SPS: inhaled or intranasal fluticasone can be used during breastfeeding; no specific infant monitoring usually needed.

src.q: When applied to the skin, inhaled or used intranasally, fluticasone can be used during breastfeeding.
No specific infant monitoring is usually required.

items.t: No human fertility data.

src.q: There are no fertility data in humans.

items.t: Very common: nosebleed (usually mild to moderate; more with use over 6 weeks). Common: nasal ulceration, headache, breathlessness.

src.q: Very common *Epistaxis Common Nasal ulceration, dyspnoea**
Common Headache.

items.t: Hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis, angioedema, rash and urticaria (rare).

src.q: Rare Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis, angioedema, rash, and urticaria.

items.t: Nasal septum perforation (very rare); growth slowing in children.

src.q: Very rare Nasal septum perforation
Growth retardation has been reported in children receiving nasal corticosteroids.

items.t: Growth in children on prolonged treatment; if slowed, reduce dose and consider referral to a paediatric specialist.

src.q: It is recommended that the growth of children receiving prolonged treatment with nasal corticosteroids is regularly monitored.

items.t: If used with a potent CYP3A inhibitor: monitor for systemic corticosteroid side effects.

src.q: in which case patients should be monitored for systemic corticosteroid side effects

items.t: Nasal use only. Shake before use. Prime with at least 6 sprays; re-prime if the cap was left off for 5 days or not used for 30 days or more. Clean after each use and replace the cap.

src.q: Avamys nasal spray is for administration by the intranasal route only.
The device is primed by pressing the mist release button for at least six spray actuations
Re-priming (approximately 6 sprays until a fine mist is seen) is only necessary if the cap is left off for 5 days or the intranasal device has not been used for 30 days or more.

items.t: Use regularly every day. It can start working within 8 hours but may take several days for full benefit.

src.q: Onset of action has been observed as early as 8 hours after initial administration.
it may take several days of treatment to achieve maximum benefit
